To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) phyA, phyAB1 and phyAB1 phyB2 mutants show delayed ripening and phyAB1 and the phyB1 phyB2 double mutant show advanced ripening; (ii) phytochrome mutants show altered accumulation of carotenoid transcripts; and (iii) phytochromes influence fruit abscission and carotenoid accumulation in tomato.
phytochromes, in addition to their role in regulating the levels of carotenoids in fruits, also play a significant role in regulating the time required for ripening.

(1) the ripening of tomato fruits is a complex process, which is regulated by a genetial hierarchy; (2) a subset of this process in tomato is modulated by light; (3) the light signal is transduced by the phytochromes; and (4) phytochromes modulate the time required for transition from one ripening phase to the next.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the complex and shifting interactions of different phytochromes in the regulation of fruit ripening.

the role of phytochroms in fruit ripening, which has not been studied before, and provides a novel perspective on the role of these light-sensing photoreceptors in the development and ripening of tomato fruits.
the elucidation of the role of phytochroms in fruit ripening and their contribution to the regulation of fruit development and ripeness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phytochromes modulate the timing of ripening and that this modulation is dependent on the phytochrome species, the ripening phase and the light environment.
phytochromes, singly and in combination, modulate ripening in a complex and dynamic way, with a phase-specific contribution to the ripening process.
phytochromes play a role in the regulation of fruit development, ripening and abscission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

phytochromes have a role in regulating the time required to complete the ripening process, but the specific contribution of individual phytochrome species depends on the ripening phase and the fruit developmental stage.
the fruit ripening process is regulated by phytochromally controlled gene expression in a phase-dependent fashion.
phyA and phyB1 are involved in the regulation of the early ripening phases, while phyB1 and/or phyB2 are involved in the late ripening phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ripening process of tomato fruits is regulated by complex and shifting interactions of multiple phytochrome species.
phytochromes, in addition to being regulators of carotenoids, also regulate the time to fruit abcsission.
phytochromes play an active role in the ripening process, not only regulating the accumulation of carotenoid pigments, but also the time required for the transition between different stages.
